title: Preserve the direction of adaptive KL learning-rate changes
body:
## Problem

PPO's adaptive schedule can reverse its intended response when an explicitly configured or restored learning rate lies outside its usual bounds:

- With `learning_rate=1e-6`, a high KL changes the rate to `1e-5`: a tenfold **increase** in the branch intended to reduce the update size.
- With `learning_rate=0.02`, a small positive KL changes the rate to `0.01`: a **decrease** in the branch intended to increase it.

These values are applied to the actual optimizer before its step, so this affects model updates, not only the reported rate.

## Changes

Bound each adaptive adjustment by the current learning rate as well as the existing floor or ceiling. A high-KL adjustment can only lower or retain the rate; a low-KL adjustment can only raise or retain it. Rates within the existing `[1e-5, 1e-2]` range keep their current behavior. A rate outside that range is retained when the existing bound would otherwise reverse the adjustment; this does not add continued scaling beyond the bounds or a new configuration option.

## Validation

The regressions collect a real rollout, shift the Gaussian policy mean to produce a measured high or low KL, and run a complete PPO update. Actor and critic parameters are compared exactly with an independent fixed-rate PPO update using the expected rate. The cases cover both inversions and both ordinary in-range directions; existing tests retain the boundary-clamping cases.

- [Original implementation with the regressions](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43910781906): **2 failed, 277 passed, 6 skipped**.
- [Fixed complete suite](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43911365103): all Python **3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12** jobs passed; the recorded Python 3.12 job reports **279 passed, 6 skipped**.
- [Lint](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43911365120), [documentation](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43911365150), and local `pre-commit run --all-files` passed.
